title: Terminal and Orbit
premise: Orsen Villalobos smuggles memories in sealed cortical drives through the contested orbits of the Meridian Gate, staying invisible by never asking what he carries. When a manifest lists him as crew on the Calypso Nine — a ship destroyed before he was born — he discovers the drives he's been hauling are fragments of a suppressed massacre that both warring factions will kill to bury. Hunted by customs, mercenaries, and his own handler, Orsen must deliver the full memory archive to the neutral arbiter station before the war's final jump window closes. He succeeds, but at the cost of his own recorded past, choosing to become the message's anonymous courier rather than its author — justice delivered by a man no one will ever remember.
about_author: Jude Quintana is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing about supply chains before turning them into interstellar crime. They live near a decommissioned airfield and write stories about people who move things they shouldn't.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He runs a routine memory-smuggling pass through Meridian customs, hiding drives inside a coffin of frozen medical samples. The beat establishes his craft, his loneliness, and the rule that keeps him alive: never open the cargo.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A broker shows him a customs record listing 'O. Villalobos' as crew on the Calypso Nine, destroyed eleven years before Orsen started flying. He laughs it off, then finds his own biometric hash in the file. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Salt in the Drives
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, first rule broken. He opens one of his own drives and experiences a fragment: a station corridor, screaming, someone with his face. The memory is dated to the Calypso Nine disaster. Beat: vertigo — the past is wearing his skin.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Ilsa Reyes, Orsen's handler, reporting to an unseen employer that the courier is compromised. She argues to protect him; the employer orders extraction 'or termination.' Beat: loyalty measured against orders.

chapters.title: Seven Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Flashback chapter: how a dockside orphan learned to hide inside other people's recorded memories, and why he erased his own childhood. Beat: sympathy — invisibility was survival, then became identity.

chapters.title: The Widow of Calypso Nine
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He tracks a survivor, Amara Osei, who confirms the massacre was real and that the 'crew' were memory couriers like him — erased and duplicated to smuggle war crimes evidence. Beat: the personal becomes political.

chapters.title: Customs Hold
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Meridian customs impounds his ship; an inspector named Duvall lets him go — too easily. Orsen realizes he's being used as bait to find the archive. Beat: paranoia tightens.

chapters.title: What the Employer Wants
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She discovers her employer is the Meridian Admiralty itself: the archive proves their flagship fired on Calypso Nine. She copies the extraction order and hesitates. Beat: complicity cracking.

chapters.title: Jump Window Math
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With Amara, he plots the only route to the neutral arbiter station — a jump window closing in nine days, through a blockade. Beat: the clock starts; dread becomes resolve.

chapters.title: The Mercenary's Offer
chapters.summary: POV of Kade Soren, a bounty hunter hired to retrieve Orsen 'alive, memory intact.' He corners Orsen in a dockside bar and offers him a way out: give up the drives, keep his life. Beat: temptation with a friendly face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen declines and barely escapes, losing his ship but keeping the drives hidden in Amara's funeral barge. Kade lets him go a beat too long. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Ilsa Defects
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She burns her handler credentials and delivers the Admiralty's extraction order to Orsen as proof. Their uneasy alliance forms over shared guilt — she built the network that erased the Calypso crew. Beat: redemption sought, not promised.

chapters.title: The Blockade Run
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A brutal passage through the picket line; Amara's barge takes damage; Orsen vents his own air supply to mask their heat signature. Beat: sacrifice as competence — he's good at disappearing.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Kade interrogates a captured dockworker and realizes the Admiralty plans to destroy the arbiter station, not just the archive. His contract suddenly looks like complicity in a massacre. Beat: the hunter's conscience turns.

chapters.title: Half a Memory
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. To decode the archive's final encryption, Orsen must interface with the drives directly — flooding his mind with the massacre and the erased couriers' lives, including the original Orsen Villalobos. Beat: identity dissolves; he learns he may be a duplicate himself.

chapters.title: The Original
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The archive reveals the truth: the real Villalobos died on Calypso Nine; Orsen is one of several copies seeded into the smuggling lanes as a living dead-drop. Beat: the book's thematic core — he was never invisible, he was never real.

chapters.title: Kade Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Kade intercepts the Admiralty strike team's orders and warns Orsen, buying them hours at gunpoint. Beat: justice outside the law requires lawless allies.

chapters.title: The Arbiter Station
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Arrival with two hours before the jump window and the Admiralty cruiser inbound. The arbiter, a cold AI-human council, demands verification — which requires Orsen to surrender his mind for full scan. Beat: the cost is named.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax. The scan begins as boarding torpedoes hit the station. Orsen holds the interface open while station defenses fight, his memories — real and inherited — streaming into the public record. Beat: self-annihilation as testimony.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The massacre plays on every open channel in contested space. The cruiser stands down; crews mutiny rather than fire. Ilsa watches the man she failed become the evidence. Beat: catharsis — the war cannot continue in daylight.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Ilsa's and Amara's POVs. Tribunals convene; the smuggling network dismantles itself; Amara buries the Calypso dead with names restored. Orsen survives the scan but with large gaps — he doesn't remember why the station matters. Beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: Terminal and Orbit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Months later, a stranger offers him a job hauling cargo through contested orbits. He accepts, keeping a single drive he chose not to surrender: the original Orsen's last recorded day, so someone carries the memory even if it isn't him. Beat: identity rebuilt as choice — he is what he carries.
